thread:
alex-cust: Hey team — starting ~2026-03-11 22:40 UTC several EU customers report ~300-600ms extra latency. Looks like traffic from Lyon is hitting our us-east edge. Example request-id: r_9f8e7d6c. Headers show `x-region: us-east-1` and p95 jumped from 30ms to 380ms. Can we triage?

nina: sorry, that's rough. Can you paste `curl -v` and a traceroute from an affected host? Also any ISP/ASN?

alex-cust: quick repro from a Lyon VM: 
```
$ curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/chat -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}
"
HTTP/2 200
x-region: us-east-1

200 0.402
```
traceroute (abridged):
1 10.0.0.1 1.1 ms
2 82.124.8.1 9.7 ms
3 34.120.9.11 395 ms
ISP ASN: 21001
```

ops-oncall: looking at infra metrics — eu region health checks had a short burst of 502/504 around 22:38-22:41 UTC. Our routing plane is configured to failover quickly (after 2 failed probes). That would move traffic to global pool (us-east). Need to check DNS answers and CDN anycast mapping.

dns-team: I ran `dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.example.com` from my laptop and got `34.120.9.11` (us-east anycast). From 1.1.1.1 I got `52.18.33.5` (eu edge). TTL is 45s currently. Looks like inconsistent DNS responses across resolvers (some POPs still prefer us-east).

cdn-vendor: we've deployed a GeoIP DB update recently (2026-03-11 21:50 UTC). We see a small set of EU edge POPs that cached stale mappings; vendor's edge geolocation cache may have been out-of-sync with origin. We're invalidating geolocation caches and pushing a rollback to previous DB while we debug.

sre: root cause triage so far: transient eu health flap + sensitive failover threshold + GeoIP/anycast inconsistency at CDN -> some clients resolved to edges that prefer us-east, causing cross-region routing. Additionally, some ISPs hold onto anycast routing longer than DNS TTL which prolongs impact.

nina: proposed immediate mitigations:
- temporarily raise DNS TTL to 300 to reduce divergent short-lived answers while vendor fixes POP mappings
- increase health-check threshold from 2->6 for eu pool for 10 minutes to avoid immediate cross-region failover
- ask CDN vendor to force-clear geolocation caches in affected European POPs and roll back the GeoIP DB change if needed

ops-oncall: executing now: raised TTL to 300 (propagates within TTL), bumped HC threshold, paused auto-failover for eu pool (15m), and opened vendor ticket CDNV-4123. Also invalidated edge geo cache where permitted.

alex-cust: happy to run more tests. From another Paris host: `dig @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.example.com` -> 52.18.33.5, `dig @1.1.1.1` -> 34.120.9.11. curl -I shows `x-region: eu-central-1` when hitting 52.18.33.5.

dns-team: that confirms inconsistent DNS view between resolvers. CDN vendor reports hotfix rolling across POPs, ETA ~10-15m. We're also preparing a short customer notice.

sre: action items logged: INF-2026-94 — rollback GeoIP DB if vendor hotfix doesn't fully clear; add pre-deploy checklist to reduce HC sensitivity during GeoIP updates; add synthetic tests for top EU ISPs to catch resolver/anycast mismatches.

nina: customer update: p95 EU latency peaked at ~420ms for ~12 minutes, ~2.1% of EU requests affected. Support sent a note to the account team.

alex-cust: seeing improvement now — recent curls return `x-region: eu-central-1` and latency back to ~35ms. Thanks for quick turnaround.

support-bot: Created INF-2026-94. Severity: P2. Link: https://issues.redwood/INF-2026-94
